page.help: Automod watches messages and joins in the main server and acts on spam, bad words, unwanted links and raids by itself, so staff do not have to catch everything. You can also change these with /automod in Discord.

topics.nowLine: What is waiting for staff at this moment.
topics.rulesLine: What automod checks, and what it does when a rule is broken.
topics.leniencyLine: Where automod looks away, and who gets a softer start.
topics.raidsLine: Checks at the door and what happens when many accounts join at once.
topics.resultsLine: How often automod acted, and how often staff undid it.

global.title: Global mode
global.help: What every rule does unless you change it below.
global.label: What automod does
global.labelHelp: Staff are told with a review card: a message in the review channel with buttons to keep or undo what automod did. In report only (don't delete) mode the card has an Apply button instead.
global.enforce: Act: delete or warn, then tell staff
global.monitor: Report only (don't delete): tell staff, do nothing

channels.title: Channels and words
channels.help: Where automod talks to staff, and your own blocked words.
channels.reviewHelp: Where staff see review cards, member reports and verifications waiting for a check. Not set: the mod log channel.
channels.alertsHelp: Where Mewvo warns staff about raids and other urgent things, and posts summaries. Not set: the mod log channel.
channels.wordsHelp: Added to the built-in bad word list. Put each word on its own line. Look-alike letters, symbols and spacing are caught too.

rules.title: Rule modes
rules.help: Change single rules. default: does what the main setting above says. on: acts. report only (don't delete): only tells staff. off: the rule is not checked. Warn privately first (2 min to fix): the first time in 30 days, the member gets a private message and 2 minutes to edit or delete the message, and nothing else happens. Personal info is removed at once without a warning. Scam, NSFW, ads, mass mentions, spam, raids and slurs always act at once.
rules.headsUp: Warn privately first (2 min to fix)
rules.headsUpUnreadable: The private first warning counts could not be read (database).
rules.headsUpCounts: Private first warnings in the last 30 days: {sent} sent, {fixed} fixed by the member, {acted} acted on after the wait.

custom.title: Custom rules
custom.help: Your own lists of words and phrases to block. Like the built-in rules, they match whole words, do not care about capital letters, and catch look-alike letters (like 0 for o). A match deletes the message and posts a review card. Warn and mute also add it to the member's record (a case). They follow the main automod setting and skip ignored channels. How many you can have depends on the server owner's plan.
custom.noPlan: Custom rules come with the Normal, Pro and Max plans. The server owner's plan counts. This server is on {plan}. {pricing}

native.title: Discord AutoMod
native.help: Discord has its own AutoMod built in. When one of its rules blocks a message, Mewvo can also log it or warn the member.
native.unreadable: Could not read Discord's own AutoMod rules. Mewvo needs the Manage Server permission for that.
native.once: At most once per member every
native.empty: This server has no Discord AutoMod rules. You make them in Discord under Server Settings, AutoMod.
native.policyHelp: ignore: nothing. log: a short line in the review channel. warn: a warning and a review card.
native.dedupeHelp: More blocks by the same member in this time are only counted. Leave empty to keep the current value.

secondChance.title: Friendly notice for a first small offence
secondChance.help: Go easy on a first small slip.
secondChance.label: Friendly notice for a first small offence: a short notice instead of a warning

mood.title: Mood
mood.help: Slowmode makes members wait a few seconds between messages.
mood.label: Mood alerts: when a channel gets heated, post a calm-down note and slow the chat for a short time

trusted.title: Trusted members
trusted.help: Trusted members skip the rules for small things. Serious rules still apply. To turn this off, pick none and set the level to 0.
trusted.roleHelp: Members with this role are trusted.
trusted.minLevelHelp: Members at this leveling level or higher are trusted too. 0 turns this off.

exceptions.title: Channel exceptions
exceptions.help: Turn one rule off, or to report only (don't delete), in one channel. For example, allow links in a links channel.
exceptions.channelHelp: A category is a folder of channels. Picking one covers every channel in it.
exceptions.modeThereHelp: off: the rule is skipped there. report only (don't delete): staff are told, nothing is deleted.

exempt.title: Ignored channels
exempt.help: Channels where automod checks nothing at all.
exempt.ignoreHelp: Automod does not check any messages here.
exempt.alsoIgnored: Also ignored (set by the bot owner outside the dashboard): {channels}

gate.title: Join gate
gate.help: Checks new members as they join. For each check: off does nothing; flag tells staff in the review channel, with Kick and Dismiss buttons; kick removes them and sends a private message saying how to come back.

checks.links: Link or invite in their name

panic.title: Panic
panic.help: A raid lockdown starts by itself when many accounts join at once. Panic mode makes it harder for raiders to spread.
panic.label: Panic mode: stop new invites and private messages between members when a raid lockdown starts

stats.undoHint: If staff undo 30% or more of a rule's actions, the rule is probably too strict.

lockdown.title: Raid lockdown
lockdown.help: A lockdown starts by itself when many accounts join at once.
lockdown.unreadable: The lockdown state could not be read (database). Reload the page to try again.
lockdown.endConfirm: End the raid lockdown? The verification level goes back to what it was and paused invites and DMs resume.
lockdown.needsAdmin: To end a lockdown you need the Administrator permission in this server.
lockdown.follow: Follow it on the raid timeline
lockdown.none: No lockdown right now. One starts by itself when many accounts join at once (a raid). Past raids are on the {timeline}.

queue.title: Review queue
queue.unreadable: The review queue could not be read (review channel unavailable).
queue.help: Review cards waiting for staff: the ones posted since the bot last started, and the last 50 messages in the review channel that still have buttons. Short lines for small things are not listed. You decide on each card in Discord with its buttons (Keep, Undo, Change, Dismiss).

probation.title: Extra-watch period after a ban
probation.help: Members who came back after a ban ended. Automod is stricter with them for a while: they skip straight to the next punishment step, and get no friendly notice or trusted-member leniency.
probation.unreadable: Extra-watch periods could not be read (database). Reload the page to try again.
probation.empty: Nobody is in an extra-watch period after a ban.

testRun.title: Test run
testRun.help: Check recent messages against your current automod settings without acting on anything. Nothing is deleted, nobody gets a message, nothing is saved or logged. Only checks that look at one message at a time run. Spam, the same text posted in many channels, and repeated insults over time are skipped, because they depend on timing. Trusted member leniency is not applied, and administrators are skipped like automod does. Messages from people who have left the server are still checked.
testRun.channelsHelp: Mewvo needs View Channel and Read Message History in each one.
testRun.howFarBackHelp: At most {max} messages in total, newest first.
testRun.draftNameHelp: Try a custom rule before you add it. It is not saved.
testRun.draftWordsHelp: One word or phrase per line, up to {max}. Matched like custom rules.
testRun.needsAdmin: To start a test run you need the Administrator permission in this server.
testRun.strictHelp: "May be too strict" shows when a rule caught at least {hits} messages, from at least {members} different members, and at least {share}% of the checked messages. It is only a hint: members may really break that rule that often. Look at the examples and the matched words before you change anything.
testRun.fixHelp: The buttons change the rule for the whole server right away, the same as the Rule modes form, and the change is logged. Report only (don't delete): staff are told, nothing is deleted. Turn on: the rule follows the main setting. Channel exceptions still apply in their channels.
testRun.skippedChecks: Not checked in a test run: Spam, the ad bot pattern (the same text in many channels from a new account), and harassment over time. An insult aimed at someone counts as Disrespect here.
testRun.strictNote: Catches a lot, may be too strict
